key_insight: Func-R1 tackles a visual-language failure mode in MLLMs: models can do the math but still miss or misread function-related visual cues, so it explicitly couples perception with theorem-level reasoning.
engineering_relevance: The paper suggests that reliable multimodal math systems should be trained with separate perception and reasoning stages rather than relying on end-to-end textual reasoning alone.
method: Decoupled architecture to separate visual evidence extraction from symbolic reasoning.
Hierarchical post-training to first identify critical visual cues, then deepen theoretical function reasoning.
Perception-Aligned Theoretic Optimization (PATO) to correct visual information during policy updates and internalize core mathematical properties.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated across diverse benchmarks and achieved state-of-the-art results among open-source MLLMs, including an 8.4% improvement over GPT-5 on MathVerse function-oriented tasks.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on explicit visual evidence alignment and staged training, performance may be sensitive to benchmark style and to failures in the perception module.
paper_title: Func-R1: Incentivizing Mathematical Function Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
